glossary.parasitic infection: Infection by an organism that lives on or inside a host and feeds off it.
glossary.endemic: Constantly present in a particular region or population.
glossary.cyclical fever: Fever that comes and goes at regular intervals, matching the parasite's red-cell cycle.
glossary.malaise: A general feeling of being unwell.
glossary.tachycardia: A heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.hypoglycaemia: Low blood glucose, here below 2.2 mmol/L.
glossary.metabolic acidosis: Too much acid in the blood from a metabolic cause, such as lactate build-up.
glossary.renal failure: Loss of kidney function so waste and fluid are not cleared.
glossary.anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.
glossary.blood smear: A drop of blood spread on a slide, stained and examined under the microscope.
glossary.gold standard: The most accurate, definitive test against which others are compared.
glossary.parasite burden: How many parasites are in the blood, shown by the thick film.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.relapse: Return of the illness after it seemed cured, here from dormant liver parasites.
glossary.dormant: Alive but inactive, able to reactivate later.
glossary.parenteral: Given by injection or infusion rather than by mouth.
glossary.blood-stage: The part of the life cycle when the parasite lives inside red blood cells.
glossary.liver stage: The part of the life cycle when the parasite multiplies inside liver cells.
glossary.endothelium: The thin layer of cells lining the inside of blood vessels.
glossary.microvasculature: The smallest blood vessels, such as capillaries and arterioles.
glossary.bilirubin: A yellow pigment made when haemoglobin is broken down; build-up causes jaundice.
glossary.gluconeogenesis: Making new glucose in the liver from non-carbohydrate sources.
glossary.insulin: The hormone from the pancreas that lowers blood glucose.
